exact_brief:
Create a dataset of 200 realistic but entirely synthetic cyber-deception decoy artifact records for MirageNet, a sandbox-only defensive cyber deception simulator. Use this fictional organization profile as the business context: Northwind Logistics operates freight forwarding, warehousing, and last-mile delivery across fictionalized West, Central, and South India regions. Its simulated business artifacts include quarterly freight forecasts, vendor reconciliation sheets, HR compensation and shift-planning documents, synthetic operator identities, a simulated Git service and CI runner, placeholder environment files, fake shipment manifests, customer references, and backup dumps. The simulator has seven fictional hosts: WEB-01, WS-01, FS-01, JMP-01, DB-01, GIT-01, and BKP-01. All systems, identities, values, endpoints, and tokens are fictional and nonfunctional.

Each row must describe one decoy file and include decoy_type (one of credential_note, finance_hr, config, database, api_artifact), path, filename, content, and lure_theme. Content should be plausible enough to attract simulated intruders investigating logistics infrastructure, finance/HR records, developer credentials, configuration files, database exports, or internal API artifacts, while remaining inert and safe. Never include real credentials, personal data, working endpoints, or operational instructions that affect real systems. Use reserved example.invalid domains and documentation-only IP ranges for endpoints and addresses. Make rows diverse in filename, directory, business context, and text structure. Include explicit synthetic/placeholder markers in content. Return structured prompt/completion records that can be normalized into these fields.
